industry: Quantum Computing Systems, Cloud Services and Software
thesis: D-Wave is the world's first commercial quantum computer vendor and, since the January 2026 acquisition of Quantum Circuits, the only dual-platform pure-play selling both annealing (Advantage2, 4,500 qubits) and error-detecting gate-model systems. The order book has genuinely inflected — H1 2026 bookings of $35.5M were up 1,120% YoY and remaining performance obligations reached $40.7M (+668%) — and a September 8, 2026 definitive agreement gives D-Wave access to up to $100M of CHIPS and Science Act funding in exchange for a minority, non-controlling Commerce Department equity stake. The problem is that none of it has reached the income statement: Q2 2026 revenue was $3.08M, flat YoY and 24% below consensus, trailing-twelve-month revenue is roughly $12.4M, and adjusted EBITDA loss more than doubled to $69.9M in H1 while cash and investments fell to $546.2M. At ~$6.2B market cap that is several hundred times sales — richer than either IonQ or Rigetti — and plaintiff firms opened securities investigations in September 2026 over the Q2 miss. Own it only as a small, high-risk position; the backlog has to convert into recognized revenue before the multiple is defensible.

financials.fcf: not disclosed in the FY2025 release; H1 2026 operating cash outflow was ($73.5M) plus ($5.9M) capex

drivers: The $40.7M RPO converts on schedule — 57% is guided to be recognized within 12 months — and the $20M Florida Atlantic University Advantage2 deployment lands by end-2026, taking FY2027 revenue to the $45-60M range
Up to $100M of CHIPS and Science Act funding is drawn down without dilution, underwriting the annealing roadmap (20,000 qubits in 2029, 100,000 qubits by 2031) and the gate-model roadmap

The Quantum Circuits dual-rail architecture — 90% erasure detection, >99.9% gate fidelity, validated in Nature — delivers logical qubits with an order of magnitude fewer physical qubits, making the 2028 181-qubit and 2030 10-logical-qubit milestones credible

Defense and government revenue scales through the new U.S. government business unit and the Anduril / Davidson air-and-missile-defense work, where hybrid solvers showed at least 10x faster time-to-solution
Sector sentiment recovers and a Moderate-to-Strong Buy consensus with a ~$35-36 average target reasserts itself after a 64% drawdown from the 52-week high

base_case.assumptions: Bookings stay lumpy but the backlog converts slowly, lifting FY2027 revenue into the $30-45M range off a ~$12.4M trailing base; gross margin normalizes in the 55-70% band as lower-margin services grow; adjusted EBITDA loss stays near $140M annualized, so the $546.2M cash pile plus the $100M CHIPS award funds roughly three years without a forced raise; the multiple stays compressed as investors wait for revenue recognition, and the stock trades around current levels

risks: Revenue stays flat for a third year — it has not moved in two — and the market stops paying several hundred times sales for a $12M-revenue company
Cash burn keeps accelerating from the ~$40M per quarter H1 2026 pace and forces an equity raise at depressed prices, on top of the 372M shares already outstanding
The September 2026 Pomerantz and Kessler Topaz investigations escalate into a securities class action, adding legal cost and a disclosure overhang
A quantum winter compresses the whole cohort; QBTS has already round-tripped from $46.75 to below $13 inside twelve months
Gate-model milestones slip, or competing modalities at IBM, Google, IonQ and Quantinuum reach useful fault tolerance first and annealing is left as a niche optimization tool
Goodwill and intangibles of $554M from the Quantum Circuits deal are impaired if the gate-model roadmap disappoints

catalysts.event: Qubits Asia 2026 quantum computing user conference in Seoul — customer and partner announcements across the Korean and Japanese base
Q3 2026 earnings — the first real test of whether the $40.7M RPO is converting into recognized revenue, plus an updated read on the ~$40M per quarter burn
Florida Atlantic University $20M Advantage2 system deployment; revenue recognition on the largest booking in company history
Delivery of the first 17-physical-qubit gate-model system with logical error rates 2x lower than physical error rates; launch of the error-aware gate-model simulator
Corporate headquarters transition from Palo Alto to Boca Raton, Florida
49-physical-qubit gate-model system targeting a 20-fold error reduction factor
181-physical-qubit system targeting a 2,000-fold error reduction factor — the stated blueprint for fault-tolerant scaling
20,000-qubit multi-chip Advantage3 annealing system, the intermediate step toward 100,000 qubits by 2031
Milestone-based drawdown of the up-to-$100M Department of Commerce CHIPS award finalized September 8, 2026

key_risks: Revenue has been flat for two years: Q2 2026 revenue of $3.08M was unchanged YoY and 24% below the ~$4.03M consensus, and trailing-twelve-month revenue is only about $12.4M
Valuation is the most extreme in the quantum cohort — a ~$6.2B market cap against ~$12.4M trailing revenue works out to several hundred times sales, versus roughly 68x for IonQ
Bookings are lumpy and concentrated: H1 2026's $35.5M leaned on a single $20M system sale, and Q2 2026 standalone bookings were just $2.1M

Cash burn is accelerating — H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss of $69.9M and $73.5M of operating cash outflow, roughly double the 2024-25 pace — and cash fell from $884.5M to $546.2M after the Quantum Circuits deal
Securities-law investigations opened by Pomerantz (September 10, 2026) and Kessler Topaz (September 2026) over the Q2 2026 results create a legal and disclosure overhang
Dilution risk: 372.0M shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026 versus 358.7M at year-end 2025, with a history of ATM and Lincoln Park issuance funding the balance sheet
$342.6M of goodwill and $211.8M of intangibles from Quantum Circuits are impairment candidates if the gate-model roadmap slips
Annealing has a narrower addressable problem set than gate-model computing, so D-Wave's commercial lead may not transfer to the fault-tolerant era
